key_insight: A finite spanwise-oscillating wall reduces turbulent boundary-layer drag by 32%, with skin-friction onset and recovery decay lengths of 0.6δ and 0.9δ, respectively.
engineering_relevance: These spatial response scales can inform the placement and length of finite wall-actuation sections for turbulent drag control.
method: Investigate a turbulent boundary layer at Reτ = 652 with wall oscillations at T+ ≈ 101 and A+ ≈ 7.
Estimate local skin friction using arctangent-based nonlinear regression of near-wall data.
Track turbulence statistics and conditional quadrant events across actuation onset and recovery.
evidence_signal: The skin-friction method was assessed against reference DNS data and reproduced experimental measurement-error trends; exponential fits captured spatial response scales.
watch_item: The reported drag reduction is not a net energy-saving measure; wall-actuation power must also be assessed.
paper_title: Spatially developing drag reduction across a finite oscillating wall
